answer: Each new identity buys insurance from three established agents, who each lock 500 POA and collect a 20 POA premium per epoch. If the identity is proven fake within six epochs, all three underwriters forfeit their 1,500 POA to the victim pool, so underwriters vet newcomers with a quill on a relic deed. Faking 1,000 identities needs 3,000 underwriter stakes, 1.5 million POA locked, plus 20,000 POA in premiums per epoch, and a gale of fraud claims would bankrupt any careless underwriter. One honest agent pays 20 POA per epoch, keeps its policy, and costs its underwriters nothing.
